title: Roslyn Analyzers
description: Enforce code quality and conventions with Roslyn code analyzers.

data.text: Roslyn Analyzers are NuGet packages that inspect your code during compilation and report diagnostics. They can warn, suggest, or even fix code issues automatically.
The .NET SDK ships with analyzers in `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers` and `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.NetAnalyzers`.
Analyzers can be configured in the `.editorconfig` file or `Directory.Build.props`.

data.title: .editorconfig Rules
data.code:
# Enforce null checks on public methods
dotnet_diagnostic.CA1062.severity = warning

# Prefer async methods for Task-returning APIs
dotnet_diagnostic.CA2007.severity = error

# Avoid empty catch blocks
dotnet_diagnostic.CA2200.severity = suggestion

data.text: Some analyzers include code fix providers that automatically fix issues. You can trigger them with the lightbulb in Visual Studio or Rider.

data.title: Example Rule: CA2007
data.code:
# CA2007: Consider calling ConfigureAwait on awaited tasks
dotnet_diagnostic.CA2007.severity = warning

terms.definition: A package that reports code issues during compilation.
A single rule reported by an analyzer with a severity level.
An automatic correction for a reported diagnostic.
A configuration file that controls analyzer severity and rules.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Treat warnings as errors in CI with `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>`.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Analyzers run at compile time and catch issues before runtime.
Configure rules in `.editorconfig` for consistent team settings.
Code fix providers can auto-resolve many warnings.
data.takeaway: Roslyn analyzers help teams maintain high code quality with minimal friction.
